- [2023/06/20] Venous thrombus typically forms in the deep veins of the legs or pelvis.
- [2023/06/20] Venous thrombus consists of platelets, fibrin, red blood cells, and leukocytes.
- [2023/06/20] Symptoms of deep vein thrombosis (DVT) include swelling, pain, warmth, and redness in the affected limb.
- [2023/06/20] Venous thrombus formation is explained by Virchow's triad: stasis of blood flow, endothelial injury, and hypercoagulability.
- [2023/06/20] Venous thrombus can lead to pulmonary embolism if the clot travels to the lungs.
- [2023/06/20] The structure of a venous thrombus changes over time, becoming more organized and fibrotic with neovascularization.
